main_text.p: fermones tuis actionibus semper respondet: Si igitur ubi liber es, ubi quod velis potes: ubi etiā vitę tuę profesio singularis famaq; verfatur, ibi uno modo semper agas, ubi judicium tuum vis existimem? Certè (opinor) in perpetua actionum, præsertim laudabiliū constantia. Hoc ufus argumēto atq; judicio P. Ramus grammaticos Donatū, Diomedem, rhetoras Quintilianum. Ciceronē, philosophos & mathematicos Aristolem, Euclidem de maximis rebus appellavit, & admonuit, magistroq; artium ufu fallaces artium institutiones plerafq; refutavit. Ponatur igitur hæc hypothesis atq; caussa: ibi Galeni judicium esse, ubi perpetuus Galeni usus, tanquā nempe perpetua approbatio fuerit. Si quis igitur de Galeni libris tam multis ullus sequatur aliam methodum, aliamq; dispositionem quàm Aristoteleam ab universalib. ad singularia: aut si quis ejus liber totus & integer, artem aliquā integram & totam, sola similitudine & dissimili tudine artificiose componat (quę prima metho dus ejus est) aut à specialissimis p media ad generalissimum artificiose progrediatur (quę copositio ejus est) aut sola consequentiū & repugnantium consideratione artificiose constituat (quæ methodus alicubi de tribus ei secūda est) aut sola comparatione majorum, minorum, parium, aut eiusdem & diversi consideratione arti ficiose cōficiat (quæ tertia) aut solo definitiōis ordine deducat (quæ de tribus postremis ultima est) ego me(ajebat P.Ramus) in Galeni sententiā authoritatemq; servum sponte devoveā. & quod

page.notes: Line numbers 5–30 are printed line-count markers in the left margin. Some words in the text are doubtful due to scan quality, notably in lines beginning "si quis ejus" and "artificiose". The final word line ("& quod") is incomplete at the page foot and continues on the next page.
